title: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 05 (Book-II & Mr. Chips High Yield)
subject: english-12

questions.question: In 'The Dying Sun', what fraction of the universe is represented by matter as compared to the immense vacuum?

options.A: Almost half of space is packed with matter.
options.B: An unimaginably tiny fraction; total matter is like a grain of sand compared to the world's beaches.
options.C: One-fourth of the universe is dense matter.
options.D: All interstellar space is filled with dense ether.

questions.explanation: The amount of solid matter in the universe is infinitesimal compared to the unfathomable empty reaches of cold space.

questions.question: Which word is synonymous with 'superstition' as discussed in 'Using the Scientific Method'?

options.A: Empirical deduction
options.B: Unfounded belief / Irrational dread
options.C: Logical hypothesis

questions.explanation: Superstition is an irrational belief arising from ignorance or fear of the unknown, unsupported by factual evidence.

questions.question: What practical prescription did Jerome's sensible doctor friend write for him?

options.A: Strong doses of arsenic, calomel, and opium
options.B: 1 lb beefsteak every 6 hours, a 10-mile walk every morning, bed at 11, and not to stuff his head with things he doesn't understand
options.C: Bed rest for two months in a darkened room
options.D: A trip to a Swiss tuberculosis sanatorium

questions.explanation: The doctor recognized hypochondria and prescribed simple food, physical exercise, regular sleep, and avoidance of medical literature.

questions.question: What physical sensation did Squire experience while peering over the parapet of Chelsea Bridge?

options.A: A sudden urge to swim in the cold water
options.B: His heart pounded wildly and he hesitated repeatedly before mustering courage to fling the sack
options.C: He fell asleep on the bridge
options.D: He began reciting poetry aloud to passersby

questions.explanation: Paralyzed by guilt and fear of watchful eyes, he repeatedly stepped back before finally pushing the sack over the parapet.

questions.question: What did the bank clerks do as Leacock rushed headlong out of the bank doors?

options.A: They called the police armed with batons.
options.B: A roar of collective laughter echoed through the vaulted ceiling of the bank.
options.C: They locked the vault doors in panic.
options.D: They ran after him to return his hat.

questions.explanation: As the revolving doors swung behind him, a deafening roar of laughter went up from the clerks who realized his hilarious mistake.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'ghastly' in the sentence: 'He had a ghastly pale face'?

options.A: Extremely pleasant and cheerful
options.B: Deathly, frightfully pale or shocking
options.C: Sunburned and radiant

questions.explanation: 'Ghastly' means causing horror, resembling a ghost, or deathly pale.

questions.question: What was the psychological toll of mirages on desert travelers as experienced by Christopher?

options.A: They provided real fresh water to drink.
options.B: They created cruel optical illusions of glistening blue lakes and palm groves that vanished upon approach, intensifying mental despair.
options.C: They cured sunburns.

questions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction creates false images of water bodies, tormenting exhausted travelers with illusory hope.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to throw someone in at the deep end'?

options.A: To teach swimming by professional coaches
options.B: To push someone into a complex, difficult situation or responsibility without adequate preparation or help
options.C: To throw money into a fountain

questions.explanation: The idiom means forcing someone to face a daunting challenge immediately with no gradual training.

questions.question: What patriotic action did Pasteur take during the Franco-Prussian War of 1870?

options.A: He volunteered to fight as an infantry rifleman despite his paralysis and returned his honorary diploma to the University of Bonn in protest against Prussian aggression.
options.B: He moved to Germany to conduct research.
options.C: He designed chemical weapons for the military.

questions.explanation: Pasteur was deeply patriotic; he tried to enlist in the National Guard and returned his Prussian honorary medical degree in moral protest.

questions.question: What fatal disease caused by hydrophobia did Pasteur overcome with his vaccine?

options.A: Rabies
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Tetanus

questions.explanation: Rabies (hydrophobia) was 100% fatal once symptoms appeared; Pasteur's post-exposure prophylaxis was a monumental breakthrough in medical history.

questions.question: What did Mustafa Kemal do with the former Ottoman Sultan Mehmed VI (Vahideddin)?

options.A: He executed him publicly in Taksim Square.
options.B: Following the abolition of the Sultanate, the discredited Sultan fled aboard a British warship (HMS Malaya) into exile in Malta.
options.C: He appointed him Minister of War.
options.D: He gave him lifetime ownership of Ankara.

questions.explanation: Recognizing that the Turkish National Assembly held all real power, the last Sultan fled aboard a British battleship into exile.

questions.question: What was the Amasya Circular of June 1919 issued by Kemal?

options.A: A declaration that the independence of the nation is endangered, and only the nation's own determination and willpower can save it
options.B: A peace treaty with Greece
options.C: An order to burn all military armories
options.D: A tax bill for agricultural wheat

questions.explanation: The Amasya Circular was the manifesto of the Turkish revolution, asserting that national sovereignty belonged to the people.

questions.question: What did Chips say to Colley's son when he entered Brookfield twenty-five years later?

options.A: 'Colley, your father was the first boy I ever punished here; he was a villain, and you are even worse!'
options.B: 'I will make you the head boy immediately.'
options.C: 'Your father owes me money.'
options.D: 'I have never heard of your family.'

questions.explanation: Chips delighted generations by recalling their fathers' schoolboy mischief with trademark dry, affectionate humor.

questions.question: What bicycle did Katherine ride that was considered progressive in the 1890s?

options.A: A safety bicycle (the new pneumatic-tired diamond frame bicycle)
options.B: A penny-farthing with a giant front wheel
options.C: A motorized tricycle

questions.explanation: The safety bicycle was the emblem of the 'New Woman' of the 1890s, allowing women independent mobility without chaperones.

questions.question: What gift did the school present to Mr. Chips on his retirement in 1913?

options.A: A cheque, a writing desk, and a silver wall clock
options.B: A sports car
options.C: A house in London

questions.explanation: Chips received a silver clock, a writing desk, and a purse from boys, masters, and alumni.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'tyrannical' as applied to Ralston's demeanor?

options.A: Despotic
options.B: Benevolent / Democratic / Mild
options.C: Dictatorial

questions.explanation: 'Tyrannical' means oppressive and autocratic; its antonym is benevolent, kind, or democratic.

questions.question: What happened to the boys Chips taught during his wartime headmastership?

options.A: They felt a unique, tender devotion toward him because his presence provided stability in a terrifying, chaotic world.
options.B: They mutinied against his Latin tests.
options.C: They all transferred to military schools.

questions.explanation: To young boys with brothers and fathers dying at the front, old Chips was a comforting rock of grandfatherly peace and sanity.

questions.question: Why did Chips say he was glad he lived into the 1930s?

options.A: Because he could watch airplanes and see a new generation carrying forward the noble spirit of England
options.B: Because television was invented
options.C: Because he hated the 19th century

questions.explanation: Chips maintained an open, gentle heart toward the modern era, seeing the eternal goodness of youth in each new decade.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'The student was accused _____ stealing the library manuscript.'

options.A: of
options.B: with
options.C: for

questions.explanation: The verb 'accuse' takes 'of' (accused of a crime), whereas 'charge' takes 'with'.

questions.question: Identify the passive form of: 'They will have finished the bridge by December.'

options.A: The bridge will have finished by them by December.
options.B: The bridge will have been finished by them by December.
options.C: The bridge will be finished by December.
options.D: The bridge would have finished by them by December.

questions.explanation: Future perfect passive requires 'will have been + past participle' ('will have been finished').
